# State-Management Checklist: Implementation-Notes Capture (ART-012)

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements governing the implementation-notes
record's own state — creation, append cadence, ordering, identity, resume, and
location over time — are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and measurable
before implementation
**Created**: 2026-08-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

Depth: standard. Audience: reviewer at PR time. Focus areas, taken from the
requesting prompt: record creation before first dispatch, append granularity per
dispatch shape, re-run state, ordering and entry identity across the lifecycle,
resume state in a fresh session or a different working copy, and location
stability once the feature directory is archived.

The sibling `error-handling.md` checklist owns the fail-open path, the gap
destination, and missing-versus-unparseable reporting fields. Those 28 items are
closed and are not re-tested here.

Run 1 found eight missing requirements, clustered into three subjects: entry
ordering, resume across working copies, and the record's life after archiving.
All eight were remediated in `spec.md`, with one supporting edit in `plan.md`,
and re-verified item by item against the amended text. The Resolutions section
at the foot records what closed each one.

## Record Creation and Header Lifecycle

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined stating the record exists, carrying its header, before the first task of Phase 7 is dispatched? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, §US1 AS-1]
- [x] CHK002 Is the create step required to run unconditionally at phase start rather than lazily on first append, so a run that dispatches nothing still leaves a record? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK003 Are the header's content and cardinality specified — exactly one, identifying the spec, written only at creation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, Contracts §Header]
- [x] CHK004 Is the header-only state specified as a legitimate terminal state rather than an incomplete one a reader should distrust? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases, Data-model §Lifecycle]
- [x] CHK005 Is the record's identity tied to the spec it names rather than to the directory that happens to hold it, so the file stays self-identifying if its path changes? [Clarity, Contracts §Header, Spec §Key Entities]

## Append Cadence and Granularity

- [x] CHK006 Are append-timing requirements stated separately for each dispatch shape rather than as one undifferentiated rule? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK007 Is the singleton and sequential branch's bound stated as immediately after the attempt completes, rather than as a vague promptness? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK008 Is the parallel branch's bound stated against an event an observer can identify — the orchestrator's next turn, and the next dispatch — so it is objectively checkable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK009 Do the stated bounds exclude batching entries to phase end, including for the last run of a phase where "before the next run is dispatched" has no next run to bound it? [Coverage, Spec §FR-003, Contracts §Append cadence]
- [x] CHK010 Are the spec's cadence bounds and the contract's cadence table consistent, with neither stricter than the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Contracts §Append cadence]
- [x] CHK011 Is the narrowed durability guarantee for a parallel run — one run's entries lost together — stated in the requirements rather than only in design rationale? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002, §Edge Cases, §Assumptions]

## Re-Run and Resume Entry State

- [x] CHK012 Are requirements defined stating a re-run appends a further entry rather than replacing the first? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, §US1 AS-5]
- [x] CHK013 Is the earlier attempt's entry required to survive a re-run unchanged? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §SC-005]
- [x] CHK014 Are requirements defined for a task re-executed by a resumed phase as distinct from a retry inside one phase, and do both produce the same additive result? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK015 Is the absence of deduplication stated as a decision rather than left to read as an omission? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]

## Ordering and Entry Identity

- [x] CHK016 Are requirements defined for the order in which entries appear in the record, or is that order described only as an incidental consequence of appending? [Resolved R1, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK017 Given entries carry no timestamp and no attempt number, is document order stated to be attempt order for two entries sharing a task ID, so a reader can tell the first attempt from the second? [Resolved R1, Spec §FR-003, §SC-006]
- [x] CHK018 Do the requirements resolve the tension between "Task IDs, not position, identify the entries" and a reader's need to use position to sequence two same-ID entries? [Resolved R2, Spec §Edge Cases, §SC-006]
- [x] CHK019 Does SC-006 cover reconstructing the sequence of attempts, or only the content of each entry taken alone? [Resolved R1, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK020 Are the ordering guarantees scoped to a single writer, given the run-state guard explicitly does not block a second run that finds one already in progress? [Resolved R3, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-003]
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements defined for entries whose task IDs no longer appear in a regenerated `tasks.md`, so the record stays readable on its own terms? [Coverage, Spec §SC-006]

## Resume and Cross-Working-Copy State

- [x] CHK022 Is what the resumed run relies on to know the record already exists stated — a check of the path itself, as against state carried in a state file, an index, or the previous session's memory? [Resolved R4, Spec §FR-002, Plan §Orchestrator file lifecycle]
- [x] CHK023 Are requirements defined for a resume in a working copy that does not carry the earlier run's record, so the outcome there is stated rather than inferred from create-if-absent? [Resolved R5, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-002]
- [x] CHK024 Is the record excluded from the state a resumed run needs in order to proceed, consistent with its exhaust classification? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities, Plan §Failure behavior]
- [x] CHK025 Are the resume requirements in spec.md consistent with the contract's lifecycle table, with neither adding a condition the other lacks? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Contracts §Lifecycle]

## Location Stability and Downstream Read Window

- [x] CHK026 Are requirements defined for the window in which downstream consumers read the record, given the feature directory is removed from active `specs/` once the spec is archived? [Resolved R6, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK027 Is the record's recoverability after that removal stated, so "downstream consumers read it later" has a defined meaning? [Resolved R6, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK028 Are the record's consumers and their read timing named, so the assumption that they can find it is validated rather than assumed? [Assumption, Spec §Key Entities, §Assumptions]

## Cross-Artifact State Consistency

- [x] CHK029 Do spec.md, `data-model.md`, and the record contract describe the same lifecycle transitions, with none carrying a state or transition the others lack? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003, Data-model §Lifecycle, Contracts §Lifecycle]
- [x] CHK030 Are the lifecycle and ordering rules stated in spec.md itself rather than only in the design artifacts that derive from it? [Traceability, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]

## Resolutions

- **R1 — entry order is a requirement, not a side effect (CHK016, CHK017,
  CHK019).** Ordering was described only in Edge Cases and `data-model.md`, both
  of which derive from spec.md rather than binding it, and SC-006 promised only
  that a reader could recover each entry's task ID and text. Nothing said a
  reader could recover the *sequence*, which is the whole question once two
  entries share a task ID. FR-003 now requires every entry to be appended after
  everything already in the record, making document order append order and
  append order collection order, and states plainly that entries carry no
  timestamp and no attempt number, so document order is the only ordering
  signal: where two entries share a task ID, the earlier-positioned entry is the
  earlier attempt. SC-006 now extends to recovering that order from the file.
  No timestamp and no attempt number was added — the entry format is settled by
  Design Concept Q1 and pinned in the contract, and the ordering already holds by
  construction. This makes it stated rather than inferred.
- **R2 — identity against position (CHK018).** The Edge Cases sentence read
  "Task IDs, not position, identify the entries", which after R1 would look like
  a disclaimer of the very property FR-003 now depends on. It meant something
  narrower: an entry's position does not encode where its task sits in the task
  list. The sentence now separates the two jobs — a task ID says which task an
  entry belongs to, position says when it was recorded — so the two requirements
  no longer appear to compete.
- **R3 — the ordering guarantee assumes one writer (CHK020).** Edge Cases claimed
  unconditionally that entries from an earlier run always precede entries from a
  later one. That holds for one writer. The run-state guard deliberately does not
  block a second run that finds one already in progress, because the state file
  carries no liveness evidence and blocking would strand every run following an
  interrupted one, so two runs against the same spec can overlap. A new
  Assumption scopes the guarantee to the single orchestrator that owns the
  phase and records that nothing coordinates concurrent writers: no lock, no
  detection, no repair. Locking was not added; it would contradict the
  no-block rule and is unjustified for exhaust.
- **R4 — what the resume checks (CHK022).** FR-002 required an existing record to
  be re-opened but never said how the phase decides one exists, leaving a
  reader free to assume run state carried the answer. It does not: the resume
  protocol reconstructs a run from the workflow file, which does not mention this
  record. FR-002 now requires existence to be determined from the record's own
  path in the working copy the run executes in, never from a state file, an
  index, or anything carried over from the session that wrote it. `plan.md`'s
  lifecycle step says the same for its "Present" branch, so the two do not drift.
- **R5 — resume in a different working copy (CHK023).** With R4 making the check
  a path check, the case where the path is empty because the run moved copies
  became answerable but was still unstated. A new Assumption states it: a
  resumed run finds a record only if its working copy holds one, the run's own
  checkpoint commits are what carry the record between copies, entries written
  since the last checkpoint exist only in the copy that wrote them, and a copy
  without the record takes FR-002's create path and starts fresh. Earlier
  entries are neither recovered nor merged, and no cross-copy reconciliation is
  specified.
- **R6 — the read window and life after archiving (CHK026, CHK027).** The spec
  pinned the record's location but never bounded how long that location holds.
  Archive cleanup removes the feature directory from active `specs/` once the
  spec is merged, which would silently invalidate any consumer expecting to read
  the record "later". A new Assumption states the path is stable for exactly as long
  as the feature directory is, that consumers read it in place during the run
  that produced it, and that after archiving the record is recoverable through
  commit history the way every other artifact in that directory is. The record
  was not relocated and no index was added: its location is settled by Design
  Concept Q8, and moving it would re-open scope for a consumer that reads it
  before archiving anyway.

## Verified without change

Three items needed reasoning rather than a citation, and each was checked
against the amended text and left alone.

- **CHK009.** FR-003's parallel bound is two clauses, not one. "Before the next
  run is dispatched" is vacuous for a phase's final run, but "no later than the
  orchestrator's next turn after that run" still binds it, so batching to phase
  end is excluded everywhere. The contract states the prohibition literally; the
  spec's bound is equivalent, so no edit was owed.
- **CHK021.** A regenerated `tasks.md` can leave entries naming task IDs that no
  longer exist. SC-006 already requires every entry to be readable from the
  record alone with no lookup against another file, so a stale ID costs a
  cross-reference, never legibility.
- **CHK024.** Key Entities classifies the record as exhaust that nothing depends
  on to make progress, which is what keeps it out of the state a resumed run
  needs. R4 and R5 stay consistent with that: a missing record is a create, not
  an error.
